I’m sorry, but I’m not interested right now in sucking it up, working through it or processing things...I just have enough energy to exist. #sicknotweak
I know others mean well when they say "hang in there", but when I'm hanging off the edge of a cliff with my energy running low "hanging in there" isn't much of an option.

I discovered that I was giving 100% of my energy to the 1% (who were never satisfied leaving me drained and ignoring the 99%). Now I work on giving 100% of my energy to the amazing 99% instead and I find myself with almost boundless energy.

It's was three years today that I tried to end my life. I'm shameful of my actions, however I will not let it define me. I work on being more in the present and not to look back in anger or look forward with anxiety (day by day, hour by hour, minute by minute). #SickNotWeak

I hear you. With my anxiety and depression, my flight, fight or freeze kicks in and I live in short-term memory land. As a result I find it hard to remember specific things as events don't pass from short-term memory to long-term memory. #SickNotWeak

I hear you. I feel with my anxiety I’m in fight/flight/freeze mode and events, conversations and moments enter short term memory, but never make it to long term memory hence the forgetfulness. #SickNotWeak

I hear you. I feel with my anxiety I’m in fight/flight/freeze mode and events, conversations and moments enter short term memory, but never make it to long term memory hence the forgetfulness. #SickNotWeak

From my experience it is the fight/flight/freeze response to anxiety that prevents any memories moving from short term to long term. The body is on high alert for any immediate threats (real or perceived) and it sacrifices remembering things in the moment to do so. #SickNotWeak

Mental illness doesn’t discriminate, however people discriminate against those with mental illness. Sometimes in my mind I feel alone even when I’m around people (and I feel all the more sad about it). I’m doing the absolute best I can, but it isn’t enough. #SickNotWeak

To help remove the stigma around #MentalIllness medications do not cure people; they help people to better handle their struggles. Another way I manage my struggles is with mindfulness. For example I know (S)tress leads to (A)nxiety which triggers my (D)epression. #Bell Lets Talk

I appreciate the increase in tweets making people aware of the importance of mental health, however I don't see much "talking" so here's actual talking: I have Major Depressive Disorder and I feel like I'm constantly drowning. #Bell Lets Talk #SickNotWeak #MentalHealthMatters
This is also a visual representation of my life right now... if I wasn't laughing, I'd be crying.

What sucks is I need my brain to do all the things I need to do to get better when said brain is also unwell. The struggle is visceral and pervasive. The other day I felt my depression as if it were sentient. I'm doing the best I can, but the world expects more. #SickNotWeak

I can understand. From my counselling I was informed that the fight/flight/freeze response inhibits the formation of long-term memories (the memories don't move from short to long-term). Ask me if I remember things from my childhood and I'm like "Nope. Don't remember".

The #WorstPartOfDepression is having a mind that is ill and needing that very same mind to try and heal it. It’s paradoxical and maddening. Oh and all the while trying to hold down a job, take care of myself and my children, maintain relationships and my health. #SickNotWeak

I keep going, forging ahead. But sometimes there are costs. My mental health, my physical health, my relationships, my finances, and my interests (among others). I only have 100% to give, but more than that is being asked for. #Depression #SickNotWeak

🖐🏻 I break down. I doubt myself. I struggle. I’m sad at times for no reason. I’m overwhelmed and I feel like I can’t cope. .....but I have to “man up”. So I’ll keep moving forward at the expense of everything else. #SickNotWeak
